title: Introduce cost-hopper batcher and quant-tier guidance
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: many tenants run conservative batch/cache/quant defaults which leave cost on the table or cause poor tail latency during bursty traffic. This PR introduces the 'cost-hopper' batcher: a lightweight policy layer that probes multiple batching shapes at runtime, hops between them to maintain latency SLOs, and surfaces per-tenant quantization tier guidance. The feature bundles three pieces: (1) cost-hopper scheduler: a tenant-scoped batching policy that dynamically selects batch shapes based on short-term latency and unit-econ signals; (2) quant-tier advisor: an offline/online guidance engine that recommends safe quantization tiers per model/tenant and produces a confidence score usable by rollout policies; (3) defaults exporter: a CLI and API to export suggested batching+cache+quant defaults as YAML for tenant onboarding. What changed: modified serving runtime scheduler to accept batching policy hooks; added a new 'cost_hopper' policy implementation with probe and decay windows; added quant-tier advisor service and an export CLI command under tools/quantcli; wired policy controls into the Console rollout UI (flags to force a policy or set sampling rate). Safety: default behavior is opt-in and sampling-only for first 24h, the policy refuses to pick quant tiers that the advisor marks 'low-confidence' unless explicitly allowed. Includes unit and integration tests and a canary rollout plan. Checklist: - implemented runtime policy, - added quant advisor and scoring, - CLI exporter and docs, - unit tests and integration tests, - perf bench and tenant-canary plan, - migration to settings API for tenant defaults. Testing summary: local unit tests and linters; synthetic perf bench against small Llama-like model; tenant canary run on staging for 48h; manual QA in Console. Related: ENG-4821 (cost-hopper design), PM-721 (defaults UX).

performance_numbers: median latency impact: +3ms on p50 for small models when sampling enabled
tail latency (p99) unchanged vs baseline due to conservative decay policy
tokens/sec (steady load): +6% throughput when cost-hopper selected compact batch shapes
estimated unit-cost reduction (sampled tenants): 9-14% depending on mix and cache hit rate
testing: integration smoke against staging cluster (48h canary)
synthetic throughput/latency bench with 1M tokens sampled

release_notes: Introduce 'cost-hopper' dynamic batching policy and quant-tier guidance. Opt-in sampling rollout only. Provides per-tenant suggested batching/caching/quant defaults exportable via tools/quantcli. Improves steady-throughput efficiency and can reduce unit cost by ~10% for compatible workloads. See docs/ops/cost_hopper_best_practices.md for rollout steps.
notes_for_ops: Default is opt-in sampling; to enable for a tenant set tenant.settings.batch_policy = 'cost_hopper' and sampling_rate <= 0.05. Migrations include adding settings key; rollback removes policy entry and reverts to tenant default batcher.
ui_changes: Console: new Policy toggle and sampling slider under Tenant > Inference Defaults. Export button in Tools panel for quant-tier suggestions.
changelog_entry: 2024-05-22: cost-hopper batcher + quant-tier advisor (opt-in) - improves cost/perf for bursty workloads; CLI export for defaults.
